key_insight: PING uses physics-informed graph learning to forecast advection-diffusion dynamics on irregular sensor networks, improving cloud-motion and solar power prediction.
engineering_relevance: The approach can help grid operators and PV plants better anticipate intra-day solar output by combining satellite cloud information with ground-based measurements.
method: Models advection-diffusion as signals on a graph for irregular spatial grids
Adds a discretized physics constraint as a soft loss term to keep predictions physically consistent
Uses the learned forecasts as input to a hybrid PV power prediction pipeline
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on synthetic and real datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, with results on par with state-of-the-art models and improved PV forecasting when coupled to sensor and satellite data.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the quality and coverage of irregular sensor and satellite data, and the physics loss must be balanced carefully to avoid over-constraining learning.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
